signals.topic: Critical runtime instability: segfaults and indefinite hangs on specific architectures
signals.summary: Goose exhibits severe stability issues including segmentation faults on ARM64 Linux when executing parallel tool calls with dependencies, and indefinite request hangs with high CPU usage on Windows

signals.topic: Cline gets stuck in infinite 'Thinking' state or loop

The core issue appears when tool_calls is null or model outputs text-only responses without tool use, causing the main workflow to completely block.
signals.review_reason: High frequency (3 issues) with complete main workflow blocking. Users cannot complete tasks when Cline enters this state, requiring manual intervention. Core functionality is severely impacted.

signals.topic: MCP tool calls fail with 'No connection found' after transient transport disconnect

signals.review_reason: Critical MCP functionality becomes completely unusable after transient disconnects. Users must start a new conversation to restore MCP tool functionality, disrupting their workflow.

source_issues.title: MCP tool calls fail with "No connection found" after transient transport disconnect
source_issues.evidence: User sees MCP server as connected in UI, but tool calls keep failing with 'Error executing MCP tool: No connection found for server: <old-uid>'. Root cause identified in McpHub.ts.

signals.review_reason: 这是长期运行场景下的真实问题，上下文窗口耗尽会影响代理的推理能力和研究效率。用户提供了具体的解决思路（子代理委托），说明问题已实际影响使用。

signals.topic: MCP tool functionality broken in CLI
signals.summary: MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration fails in CLI mode, causing ClosedResourceError during non-interactive execution and general MCP broken state, blocking users from using MCP tools entirely
signals.review_reason: Core MCP functionality blocking users from using MCP tools in CLI. Maintainer labeled P0 for internal issue, plus user-reported regression with clear reproduction steps. Two independent reports confirm this is a recurring blocking issue.

source_issues.title: MCP broken in CLI
source_issues.evidence: Maintainer-marked P0 issue indicating MCP completely broken in CLI

source_issues.title: ClosedResourceError during non-interactive execution when calling MCP tools (Regression in v0.0.34)
source_issues.evidence: User-reported regression: MCP tool calls crash CLI in non-interactive mode with ClosedResourceError, worked in v0.0.31

signals.topic: Provider package detection failures prevent CLI startup
signals.summary: CLI fails to detect installed provider packages (OpenAI, NVIDIA) despite correct installation, blocking users from starting the application at all
signals.review_reason: Complete startup failure for users - cannot even launch CLI despite following installation instructions. Two different providers affected, indicating systemic package detection issue.

source_issues.title: Error: Missing package for provider 'openai'. Install: pip install langchain-openai
source_issues.evidence: User installed langchain-openai but CLI still reports missing package, completely blocked from using CLI

source_issues.title: Bug: Missing package for provider 'nvidia' despite langchain-nvidia-ai-endpoints being installed

signals.topic: CLI crashes when displaying JSON tool output
signals.summary: MarkupError crash when tools return JSON or text with square brackets because Textual markup parser treats brackets as style tags instead of literal content
signals.review_reason: UI crash during normal operation when using tools that return structured data. Blocks workflow for users relying on JSON-returning tools like Jira integrations. Single issue but clear reproduction and user impact.

source_issues.title: MarkupError when displaying tool output containing JSON or square brackets
source_issues.evidence: Detailed reproduction: CLI crashes with MarkupError when any tool returns JSON arrays/objects. Blocks Jira/API tool usage. User provided clear stack trace and root cause analysis.

signals.topic: Skills directory parameter not recognized in create_deep_agent
signals.summary: When specifying skills parameter with directory path in create_deep_agent(), the skills are not loaded into the agent's prompt context, breaking documented functionality
signals.review_reason: SDK feature completely non-functional - users cannot use skills feature despite following API documentation. Single report but blocks important SDK capability.

source_issues.title: create_deep_agent(skills=["./skills/"]) 识别不到skill
source_issues.evidence: User provided minimal reproducible example with screenshots showing skills directory specified but not appearing in agent prompt. Core SDK feature not working as documented.

signals.topic: Shell state not preserved correctly in CLI
signals.summary: Shell environment state issues affecting command execution in CLI, linked to external report on social media
signals.review_reason: Maintainer-confirmed bug with external user evidence. Affects shell command execution reliability in CLI. Marked P2 internally.

source_issues.title: Fix shell state
source_issues.evidence: Maintainer-reported issue with social media evidence (X/Twitter link), indicating real user impact on shell command behavior

signals.topic: Streaming chunk aggregation fails for float values
signals.summary: During streaming, LangChain's merge_dicts() and _dict_int_op() functions crash when aggregating float values (e.g., logprob, cost, score fields) from LLM providers, causing streaming workflows to fail with ValueError/TypeError.
signals.review_reason: Two separate bug reports confirm that streaming crashes when LLM providers return float fields in metadata. This is a main workflow blocker affecting any user doing streaming with providers that return float values (costs, scores, logprobs).

source_issues.title: Bug: `_dict_int_op` raises ValueError for float values in UsageMetadata during streaming aggregation
source_issues.evidence: ValueError: Unknown value types: [<class 'float'>]. Only dict and int values are supported. Affects streaming scenarios where LLM providers include float fields like cost.

source_issues.title: Bug: `merge_dicts` raises TypeError for float values during streaming chunk aggregation
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: Additional kwargs key score already exists in left dict and value has unsupported type <class 'float'>. Causes stream to crash during chunk aggregation.

signals.topic: OpenAI/Azure streaming drops function_call namespace causing 400 errors
signals.summary: When using OpenAI's deferred tool loading with streaming, the namespace field is dropped from function_call content blocks during round-trip, causing API to return 400 'Missing namespace' errors.
signals.review_reason: Streaming with deferred tool loading (a new OpenAI feature) fails with 400 errors. Blocks users from using this specific OpenAI feature in production.

source_issues.title: bug(openai): Streaming drops `namespace` from deferred `function_call` content blocks, causing 400 "Missing namespace" on round-trip
source_issues.evidence: Streaming drops `namespace` from deferred `function_call` content blocks, causing 400 "Missing namespace" on round-trip. Regression from PR #35582.

signals.topic: ChatOllama crashes on Pydantic Optional fields with anyOf schema
signals.summary: ChatOllama crashes during tool binding when Pydantic models contain Optional fields, because Ollama's model templates cannot handle the anyOf: [T, null] schema pattern generated by Pydantic v2.
signals.review_reason: Users cannot use tool calling with ChatOllama when their Pydantic models have Optional fields - a very common pattern. This blocks a core feature for Ollama users.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ChatOllama crashes on Optional fields due to anyOf: [T, null] schema pattern
source_issues.evidence: Ollama's model templates expect flat schemas and do not handle the anyOf: [T, null] pattern that Pydantic v2 generates for Optional fields. This causes crashes during tool binding in ChatOllama.

signals.topic: Azure GPT-5.3-codex model not working
signals.summary: AzureChatOpenAI fails to work with the new gpt-5.3-codex model deployment, blocking users from using this model via LangChain.
signals.review_reason: Blocks users from using a specific Azure OpenAI model. May be related to model naming or API changes, but directly impacts users trying to use new models.

source_issues.title: azure gpt-5.3-codex not working
source_issues.evidence: User reports GPT-5.3-codex deployment on Azure fails to work with AzureChatOpenAI, related to issue #35584.

signals.topic: langchain-together package incompatibility with v1 langchain packages
signals.summary: langchain-together package cannot be used with v1 versions of langchain-openai and other langchain packages due to version constraint conflicts.
signals.review_reason: Package version conflicts prevent users from installing/using langchain-together with other langchain v1 packages. Blocks dependency resolution in production.

source_issues.title: langchain-together breaks with v1 versions of langchain-openai and so on
source_issues.evidence: uv sync fails: No solution found when resolving dependencies - langchain-together<=0.3.1 conflicts with traza-ai-core which requires langchain-together>=1.0

signals.topic: Background runs re-executed after ~180s causing duplicate work and wasted costs
signals.summary: Users with long-running nodes (3-7+ minutes) observe background runs being consistently re-executed after exactly ~181 seconds, even when BG_JOB_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_PERIOD_SECS is set higher. This causes duplicate API calls and wasted costs in production.
signals.review_reason: Critical production issue: Users experience duplicate execution of long-running workflows, directly causing wasted API costs and resource consumption. The issue is reproducible and has clear business impact.

source_issues.title: Background runs re-executed after ~180s despite BG_JOB_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_PERIOD_SECS being set higher
source_issues.evidence: Production workloads with long-running Anthropic API calls (3-7 min) are duplicated at ~181s, causing wasted API costs. User tried multiple configuration changes (BG_JOB_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_PERIOD_SECS=900, BG_JOB_ISOLATED_LOOPS=true) with no effect.

signals.topic: Random CancelledError in AsyncPregelLoop cleanup causing sporadic production failures
signals.summary: Users experience random asyncio.CancelledError during AsyncPregelLoop cleanup phase when running agents on LangSmith Cloud. The error occurs sporadically in production without a reliable reproduction.
signals.review_reason: Sporadic production failures that disrupt agent execution. While not blocking all usage, the unpredictable nature makes it difficult to build reliable production systems.

source_issues.title: Random CancelledError in AsyncPregelLoop cleanup
source_issues.evidence: Production users experience random CancelledError in AsyncPregelLoop cleanup. Full stack trace provided showing error originating in langgraph/pregel/_loop.py line 1323 and langgraph/pregel/_executor.py line 200.

signals.topic: ToolRuntime requirement blocks standalone tool invocation for unit testing
signals.summary: Users cannot call .invoke() on StructuredTool instances that have ToolRuntime parameters when running standalone unit tests. Pydantic rejects missing 'runtime' input and Optional[ToolRuntime] cannot be serialized to JSON.
signals.review_reason: Blocks development workflow: Users cannot write unit tests for their tools, a fundamental development practice. Forces workarounds and impacts developer productivity.

source_issues.title: Calling .invoke() as standalone on a StructuredTool requires a ToolRuntime object
source_issues.evidence: User cannot unit test tool functions because invoke() requires ToolRuntime object. Pydantic validation fails with 'runtime input is missing' and Optional[ToolRuntime] fails JSON serialization check.

signals.topic: ModuleNotFoundError prevents langgraph dev startup with latest Docker image
signals.summary: langgraph dev fails on startup with ModuleNotFoundError for langgraph_executor module in langgraph-api 0.7.35 Docker image. The queue entrypoint crashes in a loop, preventing application startup.
signals.review_reason: Startup crash: Users cannot run langgraph dev with latest Docker image. Issue is closed which may indicate fix, but represents a real pain point for users who encountered this regression.

source_issues.title: langgraph dev: ModuleNotFoundError for langgraph_executor in langgraph-api 0.7.35 Docker image
source_issues.evidence: Docker image langchain/langgraph-api:3.11 missing langgraph_executor module. Verified via docker exec that module does not exist. Full traceback shows import failure in executor_service.py line 13.

signals.topic: Map-reduce state with tuple keys breaks LangSmith tracing
signals.summary: When LangGraph state contains dict with tuple keys (e.g., dict[tuple[str, str], str]), LangSmith traces fail to complete with serialization errors. Graph executes successfully but observability is lost.
signals.review_reason: Loss of observability for specific state patterns. While graph execution succeeds, users lose tracing capability which is critical for debugging and monitoring production systems.

source_issues.title: Map-reduce fails to trace when reducing dictionary with tuple keys
source_issues.evidence: Minimal reproducible example provided. Error: 'keys must be str, int, float, bool or None, not tuple'. Traces show as 'running' indefinitely. User provided workaround using list[tuple] instead.

signals.topic: Knowledge base retrieval and document management failures
signals.summary: Knowledge base functionality experiences multiple issues including Weaviate connection drops after idle periods, document updates stuck in queuing status, and inconsistent document status display between list and detail pages
signals.review_reason: User pain point with clear functional impact: Knowledge base is a core Dify feature. Users cannot reliably retrieve knowledge after idle periods, update documents via API, or trust status displays. Three independent reports validate this is a recurring issue pattern.

source_issues.title: The `WeaviateClient` is closed. Run `client.connect()` to (re)connect!
source_issues.evidence: Knowledge base recall test fails after 2 hours of idle time. Weaviate Python SDK v4 closes connections but is_ready() check doesn't trigger reconnection.

source_issues.title: The document update via API is stuck in the queuing status.
source_issues.evidence: Document update via API stuck in queuing status. Worker logs show task received but no progress after indexing cleanup.

source_issues.title: document detail page status inconsistency with list page
source_issues.evidence: Document list shows 'Available' but detail page shows still 'Indexing'. Status inconsistency confuses users about actual document state.

signals.topic: Version upgrade breaks existing applications and plugin functionality
signals.summary: After upgrading Dify or Agent strategy plugins, existing chatflow applications and stream output functionality break unexpectedly, causing LLM node failures and degraded user experience
signals.review_reason: High-impact pain point: Users cannot safely upgrade without breaking existing applications. Two independent reports of upgrade-related failures affecting core functionality (LLM nodes and stream output). Blocks production usage and creates fear of upgrades.

source_issues.title: After upgrading to version 1.13.1, the original chatflow application LLM node cannot operate normally
source_issues.evidence: PluginInvokeError after upgrade: 'Object of type TextPromptMessageContent is not JSON serializable'. User cannot rollback and has many applications affected.

source_issues.title: Why the latest Dify Agent strategy plugin can not support stream output?
source_issues.evidence: After upgrading plugin from 0.0.31 to 0.0.33, stream output stopped working - users see no output until final result appears suddenly. User explicitly stated 'It very very really bad feeling!'

signals.topic: Self-hosted deployment failures - permission and SSL errors
signals.summary: Users encounter deployment blockers including PermissionError on startup and SSL certificate verification failures when running Dify in self-hosted Docker environments
signals.review_reason: User pain point blocking initial setup: New users trying to self-host Dify encounter deployment failures that prevent them from even starting to use the product. This blocks adoption and creates negative first impression.

source_issues.title: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied
source_issues.evidence: Service fails to start with PermissionError. User tried various methods but cannot resolve the problem.

source_issues.title: The same networks=default was used, ssl failed
source_issues.evidence: SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED - self-signed certificate error when running with default network configuration.

signals.topic: Cloud workflows completely non-functional - zero execution, zero logs
signals.summary: Pro account users experience complete workflow failure on Dify Cloud - all workflows fail instantly without node execution or log entries, regardless of execution method (API, workflow-as-tool, or UI)
signals.review_reason: Critical user pain point: Pro subscriber's entire workflow system is completely blocked. Main workflow execution path is broken with zero workaround. Strong evidence of production impact affecting paid users.

source_issues.title: [Bug][Cloud] All workflows completely non-functional — zero node execution, zero logs, instant failure (Pro account)
source_issues.evidence: Every workflow in workspace fails instantly, no node ever starts execution, no log entries recorded. Paid Pro subscriber affected. Issue started suddenly without any config changes.

signals.topic: Workflow execution hangs without response or error
signals.summary: Workflows run continuously without producing any response or error messages, leaving users unable to determine what went wrong or how to recover
signals.review_reason: User pain point affecting workflow reliability: When workflows hang silently, users lose confidence in the system and cannot debug issues. Lack of error reporting makes this particularly frustrating.

source_issues.title: The workflow is running continuously without any response.
source_issues.evidence: Workflow and Q&A are unresponsive and won't proceed without reporting any errors. User cannot determine cause or resolution.

signals.topic: Graph memory silently fails with non-OpenAI LLM providers (Ollama, Google/Gemini) - tools parameter not passed
signals.summary: When using Ollama or Google/Gemini as LLM providers with graph memory enabled, entity extraction silently produces zero results. The LLM wrappers don't pass the tools parameter to the underlying API, causing graph memory operations to fail without any error messages.
signals.review_reason: Core graph memory functionality completely broken for non-OpenAI LLM providers. Users enable graph memory and expect entities to be extracted, but get zero results with no error indication. High frequency (3 distinct issues) affecting a key feature. Silently broken functionality causes confusion and wasted debugging time.

source_issues.title: OllamaLLM never passes tools to Ollama — graph entity extraction silently fails
source_issues.evidence: Graph memory entity extraction silently produces zero results when using Ollama. The Ollama wrapper drops tools parameter. After fix, 6 entities correctly extracted.

source_issues.title: GoogleLLM.generateResponse ignores tools parameter — graph memory silently produces no entities
source_issues.evidence: Graph memory operations return plain text, zero entities extracted, Neo4j never populated. No error thrown; failure is completely silent.

source_issues.title: KeyError for entities during retrieval
source_issues.evidence: KeyError: 'entities' during memory retrieval, blocking the search operation.

signals.topic: Qdrant vector store configuration and authentication issues - wrong dimensions, JWT incompatibility
signals.summary: Multiple issues with Qdrant integration: defaulting to 1536 dimensions instead of detecting embedder dimensions, and throwing 403 errors when using collection-scoped JWTs because only 409 conflict is caught.
signals.review_reason: Qdrant is a popular vector store choice. Wrong dimension defaults cause storage failures that are hard to diagnose. JWT authentication issue blocks users following security best practices. Both issues directly prevent memory storage operations.

source_issues.title: Qdrant collection created with wrong vector dimensions — mem0 defaults to 1536
source_issues.evidence: Mem0 defaults to 1536 (OpenAI embedding size) when creating collection, even when using nomic-embed-text (768 dims). Causes vector storage failures.

source_issues.title: ensureCollection throws 403 with Qdrant scoped JWTs — only catches 409
source_issues.evidence: When Qdrant configured with collection-scoped JWT, createCollection returns 401/403. Only 409 is caught, so every write operation throws.

signals.topic: OpenMemory UI/Docker issues - HTTPS proxy stats failure, env vars ignored
signals.summary: OpenMemory deployment issues: stats widget shows 0 behind HTTPS reverse proxy due to trailing-slash redirect causing mixed-content block, and Docker Compose environment variables are ignored since config is stored in SQLite.
signals.review_reason: Self-hosting is a common deployment pattern. These issues break the OpenMemory dashboard experience and make Docker-based configuration non-functional. Users following documented setup instructions get broken deployments.

source_issues.title: OpenMemory: Stats widget shows 0 when deployed behind HTTPS reverse proxy
source_issues.evidence: Stats widget shows 0 Memories/0 Apps. Browser blocks https:// to http:// downgrade as mixed-content violation.

source_issues.title: Docker Compose env vars (LLM_PROVIDER, OLLAMA_BASE_URL, etc.) are ignored
source_issues.evidence: Config stored in SQLite DB, not read from environment variables. .env file only matters for initial startup check.

signals.topic: Dependency version conflicts - protobuf v6.x incompatible, langchain-neo4j 0.7.0 parameter mismatch
signals.summary: Two dependency compatibility issues: protobuf pinned to <6.0.0 conflicts with projects requiring protobuf 6.x; langchain-neo4j 0.7.0 changed parameter order causing Neo4jGraph instantiation failures with positional arguments.
signals.review_reason: Blocks installation or causes runtime errors when mem0 is integrated into projects with modern dependency versions. Users cannot resolve dependencies without workarounds. Lower priority as workarounds exist (forcing versions, using keyword args).

source_issues.title: Widen protobuf constraint to support v6.x
source_issues.evidence: Current protobuf>=5.29.0,<6.0.0 constraint causes dependency conflicts when integrating with projects requiring protobuf>=6.0.0.

source_issues.title: langchain-neo4j >=0.7.0 compatibility bug: Neo4jGraph instantiation fails
source_issues.evidence: langchain-neo4j 0.7.0 added token parameter between password and database. Positional args cause database value assigned to token parameter.

signals.topic: Timestamp timezone hardcoding (US/Pacific) breaks date-range filtering and multi-tenant deployments
signals.summary: created_at and updated_at timestamps are hardcoded to US/Pacific timezone instead of UTC, causing date-range filters to return incorrect results and breaking multi-tenant global deployments where timestamps appear in wrong calendar dates.
signals.review_reason: Core data integrity issue affecting any user doing time-based queries. Date-range filtering is a fundamental feature that returns wrong results. Impacts all non-Pacific timezone users. Clear user impact with data correctness problems.

source_issues.title: Bug: `created_at` and `updated_at` hardcoded to US/Pacific instead of UTC
source_issues.evidence: Date-range filters break. Memory created at UTC midnight appears as previous day Pacific. Multi-tenant/global deployments fundamentally broken. Related to issues #3036 and #3213.

signals.topic: Workflow with Handoff orchestration fails on session restore
signals.summary: Users attempting to use Workflow as Agent with Handoff orchestration in Web API scenarios encounter InvalidDataException on subsequent requests. The first request works but the second fails with 'The specified checkpoint is not compatible with the workflow associated with this runner'.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断 - 用户在 Web API 场景中使用 Workflow with Handoff 时，第一次请求正常，第二次请求因 checkpoint 不兼容而失败，导致会话恢复完全不可用。

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: InvalidDataException when using Workflow as Agent with Handoff orchestration
source_issues.evidence: User trying to create a Workflow using an Agent with Handoff in Web API application. First request works, second fails with InvalidDataException when restoring checkpoint.

signals.topic: Unable to install agent-framework on ARM64 architecture
signals.summary: Users on Windows 11 ARM64 (Snapdragon X12) cannot pip install agent-framework due to missing wheel packages for cryptography, aiohttp, httptools, grpcio dependencies on Python 3.12/3.13.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用 - ARM64 用户完全无法安装框架，阻止了整个用户群体使用该产品，用户被迫使用 codespaces 作为变通方案。

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Impossible to install agent-framework on ARM64
source_issues.evidence: User on Windows 11 ARM64 unable to install framework, tried both Python 3.12 and 3.13, had to move to codespaces as workaround.

signals.topic: OpenAI Responses API 400 error on multi-turn conversations with previous_response_id
signals.summary: Multi-turn conversations fail with 400 invalid_prompt error when using previous_response_id. The Responses API expects only system/developer/user messages but the framework sends full history including assistant messages.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断 - 使用 OpenAI Responses API 的多轮对话功能完全失败，导致用户无法进行正常的多轮会话。

source_issues.title: Python: Fix OpenAI Responses API 400 error when using previous_response_id with assistant messages
source_issues.evidence: Multi-turn conversations using OpenAI Responses API fail with 400 error when previous_response_id is used.

signals.topic: A2AAgent fails to parse message content from TaskStatusUpdateEvent
signals.summary: A2AAgent cannot correctly extract message content from TaskStatusUpdateEvent when the A2A Server sends messages with text_content in the status message field.
signals.review_reason: 功能不可用 - A2AAgent 无法正确解析服务器发送的消息内容，影响 A2A 协议的正常使用。

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: A2AAgent failed to parse message content from TaskStatusUpdateEvent
source_issues.evidence: A2AAgent fails to extract message content correctly from TaskStatusUpdateEvent when server sends messages in standard format.

signals.topic: ChatMiddleware bypassed when submitting tool results
signals.summary: ChatMiddleware is only called for the initial message but not when tool call results are sent back to the model, breaking middleware-based logging and instrumentation use cases.
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降 - 中间件机制不完整，工具调用后的消息绕过中间件，影响日志记录、监控和自定义处理等关键功能。

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: ChatMiddleware isn't called when submitting tool results back to the model
source_issues.evidence: First message goes through middleware correctly, but tool call results get sent to model without passing through ChatMiddleware.

signals.topic: AutoGen Studio silently drops extra_body config for OpenAI-compatible endpoints
signals.summary: When configuring OpenAIChatCompletionClient through AutoGen Studio's JSON editor with extra_body field (e.g., for vendor-specific parameters like enable_thinking for Qwen3), the field is silently dropped during deserialization. This prevents users from passing required parameters to OpenAI-compatible endpoints, causing BadRequestError failures.
signals.review_reason: Real user pain point where configuration is silently ignored, leading to workflow failures when using OpenAI-compatible endpoints with vendor-specific parameters. User provides clear reproduction steps and error evidence.

source_issues.title: extra_body in OpenAIChatCompletionClient config is silently ignored when loaded via AutoGen Studio JSON
source_issues.evidence: User reports that extra_body field is silently dropped when loading config via AutoGen Studio, causing BadRequestError when calling Qwen3 models. The same configuration works correctly when instantiated directly via Python.

signals.topic: OpenAIClient.message_retrieval fails to handle list content from reasoning models
signals.summary: When using OpenAI-compatible APIs with reasoning models (GPT-5, o1), the Chat Completions API returns message.content as a list of content blocks with types like 'reasoning' and 'text'. OpenAIClient.message_retrieval returns this list unchanged, causing empty or malformed responses because downstream code expects a string.
signals.review_reason: Real functional bug affecting users of new reasoning models. Core API integration fails to properly handle response format, causing workflow failures. Will become more impactful as reasoning model adoption increases.

source_issues.title: PyAutoGen Reasoning Content
source_issues.evidence: User reports that using reasoning models (GPT-5, o1) results in empty or malformed responses because message_retrieval does not normalize list content to string by extracting text from blocks.

signals.topic: RequestUsage missing costs and cached tokens tracking from v2
signals.summary: The RequestUsage dataclass in v4 only includes prompt_tokens and completion_tokens, missing important fields like costs and cached tokens that were available in v2. This regression makes it difficult for users to track API costs and caching efficiency.
signals.review_reason: Regression from v2 affecting production users who need to monitor API costs. Multiple related issues cited (#4769, #4719). Real pain point for enterprise users requiring cost visibility.

source_issues.title: Model Costs and Cached Tokens
source_issues.evidence: User reports that v2 had client.total_usage_summary and planner.client.actual_usage_summary with token counts and costs. v4's RequestUsage dataclass lacks costs and cached tokens, making it impossible to track API spending.

signals.topic: Test runner hangs indefinitely and does not exit after tests complete
signals.summary: Users report that Playwright test runner fails to exit after tests complete, causing CI/CD pipelines to hang and timeout. The issue manifests when chrome-headless-shell doesn't exit after Browser.close via CDP, or when Chrome spawns background processes (GoogleSoftwareUpdate, chrome_crashpad_handler) that inherit stdio pipes and prevent the close event from firing.
signals.review_reason: Critical user pain point: Tests complete successfully but CI/CD pipelines hang indefinitely waiting for the test runner to exit. This causes significant disruption to development workflows, wastes CI resources, and requires manual intervention or forced timeouts. Multiple independent reports confirm this is a recurring issue in production CI environments affecting teams running thousands of tests daily.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Playwright randomly not exiting
source_issues.evidence: User reports this happens 30-100 times a day across thousands of CI runs with 10 parallel workers. Chrome-headless-shell doesn't exit after Playwright sends Browser.close via CDP. Worker's fixture teardown blocks waiting forever for process close event. CI step eventually times out.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Test runner hangs indefinitely on browser.close() in macOS when using channel: 'chrome' due to inherited stdio pipes
source_issues.evidence: Terminal output stops after tests finish executing. Parent process and test workers hang indefinitely instead of generating report and exiting. Background Chrome processes (GoogleSoftwareUpdate, chrome_crashpad_handler) inherit stdout/stderr pipes and keep them open, preventing 'close' event emission.

signals.topic: HTML reporter does not open when running tests through JetBrains IDEs
signals.summary: After version 1.57, the HTML reporter fails to open automatically when running Playwright tests through WebStorm, IntelliJ, or other JetBrains IDEs. The regression was caused by a change that checks for TTY availability, which is undefined in IDE environments.
signals.review_reason: User pain point: Users relying on JetBrains IDEs for test development cannot view HTML test reports after tests complete. This breaks the expected workflow and forces users to manually locate and open report files. The issue is a clear regression that affects a significant user segment using JetBrains IDEs.

source_issues.title: [Regression]: HTML reporter does not open anymore after executing test through WebStorm/Intellij test runner
source_issues.evidence: HTML reporter doesn't open test report when running playwright tests through WebStorm / Intellij / JetBrains IDEs. This regression started from v1.57 and was caused by a PR that checks TTY status. The issue prevents users from viewing test results in the HTML report format.

signals.topic: Firefox page.reload() sends GET instead of re-POSTing form submission pages
signals.summary: In Playwright's Firefox browser, page.reload() incorrectly converts a POST request to GET when reloading a page reached via form submission. This differs from Chromium behavior and standard browser behavior where window.location.reload() re-POSTs the form data.
signals.review_reason: User pain point: Cross-browser test inconsistency where Firefox's page.reload() behaves differently from Chromium and from native Firefox browser. This causes test failures for users testing form submission workflows across browsers, requiring workarounds or browser-specific test logic. The behavior is clearly incorrect as it differs from both the native browser and Playwright's Chromium implementation.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Firefox Page.reload() sends GET instead of re-POSTing a form submission page
source_issues.evidence: Comprehensive reproduction shows Chromium correctly re-POSTs on page.reload(), but Firefox incorrectly sends GET. This breaks tests that need to verify form submission behavior and reload functionality. The issue is specific to Playwright's Firefox implementation as native Firefox window.location.reload() correctly re-POSTs.

signals.topic: Vector database connector version incompatibility breaks runtime
signals.summary: Users experience runtime crashes when using newer versions of database drivers (Npgsql 10.x, Qdrant 1.17+) with Semantic Kernel vector store connectors due to breaking API changes
signals.review_reason: Both issues cause runtime failures that block vector database operations - a core feature for RAG applications. Users combining SK with Entity Framework or upgrading Qdrant encounter unexpected crashes.

source_issues.title: Bug: System.MissingMethodException: 'Method not found: 'System.Threading.Tasks.Task Npgsql.NpgsqlConnection.ReloadTypesAsync()'.'
source_issues.evidence: Runtime crash on CollectionExistsAsync() when using Npgsql 10.0.2 with PgVector connector - MissingMethodException thrown

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Wrong input: Vector dimension error: expected dim: 3072, got 0 with qdrant server 1.17.0
source_issues.evidence: GrpcException with Qdrant 1.17.0 due to gRPC API changes causing vector dimension errors on upsert operations

signals.topic: MCP connection hangs indefinitely on auth failures
signals.summary: MCPStreamableHttpPlugin does not treat HTTP 401/403 as fatal errors, causing connections to hang forever instead of failing fast with proper error messages
signals.review_reason: Blocks MCP integration completely - users cannot connect to MCP servers when authentication fails, and get no useful error message. Debugging is difficult as it appears to be a timeout rather than auth issue.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: MCPStreamableHttpPlugin.__aenter__() method doesn't treat HTTP 401/403 as fatal errors
source_issues.evidence: When MCP server returns HTTP 401, the exception handler raises error but doesn't set ready_event, causing connect() to hang forever waiting for the event

signals.topic: Streaming agent responses duplicate content with tool calls
signals.summary: InvokeStreamingAsync concatenates pre-tool-call text with post-tool-call reply in chat history, corrupting conversation state
signals.review_reason: Corrupts chat history which affects subsequent turns in multi-turn conversations. Agents with tool calling capability are a core feature, and this breaks conversation fidelity.

source_issues.title: .Net Bug: `InvokeStreamingAsync` duplicates assistant response when tool calls are used
source_issues.evidence: Chat history shows merged text (initial 'I'm going to pull...' + final answer) instead of separate messages matching OpenAI API responses

signals.summary:
Prompts containing HTML tags like

are blocked by Semantic Kernel, preventing legitimate use cases involving HTML content
signals.review_reason: Blocks legitimate use cases where users need to process or translate HTML content. Content filtering is overly aggressive without user control.

source_issues.title:

getting blocked in Semantic Kernel version 1.39.4

signals.topic: SQLite vector extension unavailable on Alpine Linux
signals.summary: vec0.so extension cannot be loaded on Alpine Linux 3.22, preventing SQLite vector store usage in Alpine-based containers
signals.review_reason: Blocks deployment to Alpine-based Docker containers, a common production environment. Users must switch to Debian-based images or find alternative vector stores.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.SqliteException – Error loading shared library vec0.so on Alpine 3.22
source_issues.evidence: SqliteException thrown when LoadExtension('vec0') is called on Alpine 3.22 - shared library not found

signals.topic: Repeated approval prompts and sandbox permission loops blocking workflow
signals.summary: Users experience repeated approval prompts despite selecting 'don't ask again', causing workflow interruption and frustration. The sandbox escalation system fails to remember previous approvals, particularly affecting subagents and MCP tools like Playwright.
signals.review_reason: High-frequency issue (4 reports) directly blocking main user workflows. Users cannot work efficiently as they must repeatedly approve the same actions. Regression from v0.114 to v0.115/v0.116 confirms this is a new bug affecting production users.

source_issues.title: v0.116 repeatedly prompts for escalation on same file despite "don't ask again"
source_issues.evidence: Selecting 'don't ask again for these files' does not suppress next prompt on same file. Works in v0.114.

source_issues.title: CLI 0.116.0: Approval prompt shown for almost every command
source_issues.evidence: Approval prompts appear for almost every command, problem persists from v0.115.0 to v0.116.0. Works in v0.114.0.

source_issues.title: Bug subagents/multiagents ubuntu
source_issues.evidence: Subagent keeps asking for permission endlessly even after granting all permissions.

source_issues.title: Codex App for macOS: Playwright MCP no longer offers or remembers "approve for this session"
source_issues.evidence: After app update, Playwright MCP requires manual approval for every action instead of honoring session-scoped approval.

signals.topic: Model selection not preserved for subagents and conversation continuation
signals.summary: When spawning subagents or resuming conversations, Codex fails to preserve the explicitly selected model and model_provider settings. This causes wrong model execution, encrypted content errors, and unexpected cost/behavior.
signals.review_reason: Clear user impact: cross-provider conversations break with encrypted content errors, and cost-sensitive subagent delegations cannot be trusted. Multiple reports confirm the issue affects both CLI and App across model selection scenarios.

source_issues.title: thread/resume does not restore model_provider from persisted metadata
source_issues.evidence: Resuming conversation sends encrypted_content to wrong API endpoint, producing invalid_encrypted_content error. model_provider not restored during resume.

source_issues.title: spawn_agent(model="gpt-5.4-mini") produces child thread metadata with model="gpt-5.4"
source_issues.evidence: Subagent spawned with gpt-5.4-mini is recorded as gpt-5.4 in metadata, making it impossible to verify model selection and cost.

source_issues.title: spawn_agent should preserve explicit model overrides for explorer agents
source_issues.evidence: spawn_agent with explicit model override falls back to default model instead of using requested model.

signals.topic: Windows App crashes and environment corruption
signals.summary: Windows Codex App experiences startup crashes due to sandbox ACL setup failures on protected WindowsApps paths, and shell child processes receive corrupted PATHEXT environment variable, breaking git/cmd commands.
signals.review_reason: Windows-specific but severe: one issue causes app crashes making Codex unusable, the other breaks basic shell tool execution. Both directly impact user's ability to use Codex on Windows platform.

source_issues.title: Windows Store Codex App crashes after update: sandbox ACL setup fails on WindowsApps path
source_issues.evidence: App crashes during startup with 'SetNamedSecurityInfoW failed: 5' when trying to grant ACLs on protected WindowsApps path.

source_issues.title: [Windows Desktop] Shell child processes get PATHEXT truncated to .CPL
source_issues.evidence: PATHEXT truncated to .CPL breaks bare executable names like git, cmd. Direct full-path execution still works, confirming environment corruption.

signals.topic: Session context tracking failures
signals.summary: Codex loses track of active task context during long sessions, returning to previously completed tasks. CLI also hangs indefinitely when network changes during requests.
signals.review_reason: Context tracking failure causes wrong file edits in long sessions, which is a significant safety concern. Network hang makes CLI unusable without restart in common VPN scenarios.

source_issues.title: Codex gets lost in the middle of an execution and returns to a context that had already been closed
source_issues.evidence: After topic switch acknowledged by Codex, a short confirmation caused it to resume previous completed task and edit wrong files.

source_issues.title: Codex CLI request hangs on network change (VPN disconnect)
source_issues.evidence: CLI stays in 'working' state indefinitely after VPN disconnect, failing to error or recover.

signals.topic: API request errors with invalid parameter patterns
signals.summary: Users encounter invalid_request_error with parameter validation failures after any prompt in some conversations, making those threads unusable.
signals.review_reason: Single report but completely blocks the affected conversation threads. Error pattern suggests a systematic issue with parameter name generation that could affect more users.

source_issues.title: invalid_request_error after any prompt in some conversations
source_issues.evidence: Error 'input[71].name does not match pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$' appears after every prompt in affected conversations, blocking all work.

signals.topic: Handoff 与 server-managed conversation 不兼容导致 API 错误
signals.summary: 使用 handoff（特别是 remove_all_tools 或 nest_handoff_history）与 conversation_id/previous_response_id 组合时，会导致 API 400 错误或结果不正确。根本原因是 SDK 内部修改了聊天历史，但服务器端对话历史未同步修改。
signals.review_reason: 用户使用 handoff 和 server-managed conversation 的标准组合时遇到 API 400 错误，这是主流程阻断问题，有完整复现步骤和错误日志证据

source_issues.title: nest handoff: Handoff is incompatible with server-managed conversation
source_issues.evidence: 用户提供完整复现代码，运行时产生 openai.BadRequestError: No tool output found for function call 错误，以及 nest handoff history 与 conversation_id 组合导致结果不正确

signals.topic: SQLAlchemySession 并发首次写入丢失数据
signals.summary: SQLAlchemySession 在多个任务同时首次写入同一新会话时存在竞态条件，导致 OperationalError（表已存在）或 IntegrityError（唯一约束失败），部分写入丢失，会话历史不完整。
signals.review_reason: 并发场景下会话数据丢失，直接影响用户数据的完整性和可靠性，属于主流程失败

source_issues.title: SQLAlchemySession can fail and drop writes on concurrent first access
source_issues.evidence: 用户提供最小复现代码，25个并发写入最终存储项数量远少于提交数，并明确指出两个竞态条件位置

signals.topic: Traces 仪表板大整数参数显示截断
signals.summary: 在 OpenAI platform traces dashboard 中查看工具调用追踪时，超出 JS number 精度范围的大整数参数会被截断显示，导致调试时看到的数值与实际传递的不一致。
signals.review_reason: 影响调试体验，用户在排查问题时看到错误数值会产生困惑，但非主流程阻断

source_issues.title: Traces dashboard shows big integer arguments incorrectly in tool calling traces
source_issues.evidence: 用户提供截图对比：SDK 正确传递 10000000000000001，但 dashboard 显示为截断值

signals.topic: MCP StreamableHttp 不暴露 session ID
signals.summary: MCPServerStreamableHttp 类未暴露底层 streamablehttp_client 返回的 session_id，导致用户无法在无状态架构或多次请求间维持有状态的 MCP 会话。
signals.review_reason: 限制用户在无状态 worker 架构中使用有状态 MCP 会话的能力，影响生产部署灵活性

source_issues.title: OpenAI SDK does not expose MCP session ID, making stateful streamable HTTP sessions impossible
source_issues.evidence: 用户展示代码验证 session_id 属性不存在，指出 SDK 丢弃了 get_session_id 回调，并提供了解决方案建议

signals.topic: Empty OPENAI_BASE_URL environment variable prevents fallback to default endpoint
signals.summary: When OPENAI_BASE_URL is set to an empty string, the SDK does not fall back to the default API endpoint, causing APIConnectionError instead of using https://api.openai.com/v1
signals.review_reason: Causes connection errors that block API usage when environment variable is accidentally set to empty. Common in containerized/dev environments where env vars may be initialized but empty.

source_issues.title: Empty OPENAI_BASE_URL prevents fallback to default API endpoint
source_issues.evidence: User reports that export OPENAI_BASE_URL="" followed by client.models.list() triggers openai.APIConnectionError: Connection error, because the fallback logic only checks for None, not empty strings

signals.topic: prompt_cache_retention type definition uses hyphen but API expects underscore
signals.summary: SDK type stubs declare prompt_cache_retention with Literal["in-memory", "24h"] but the actual API only accepts "in_memory" (underscore), causing 400 Bad Request errors when using the SDK-typed value
signals.review_reason: Type-level bug causes all API calls using prompt_cache_retention with SDK-typed values to fail with 400 errors. Requires type checker suppression workaround, undermining type safety benefits.

source_issues.title: `prompt_cache_retention` type declares `"in-memory"` but API expects `"in_memory"`
source_issues.evidence: Detailed PoC shows SDK accepts 'in-memory' per type stubs but API returns 400 Bad Request. User must use 'in_memory' with type: ignore workaround to bypass type checker

signals.topic: Custom API base URL requests return 'Your request was blocked' error
signals.summary: Users configuring custom base_url encounter 'OpenAIException - Your request was blocked' even when the same endpoint works with direct HTTP requests via requests library
signals.review_reason: Blocks users from using custom/proxy API endpoints with the SDK, forcing fallback to raw HTTP clients. Lower confidence due to limited reproduction details, but indicates real integration pain for enterprise proxy scenarios.

source_issues.title: OpenAIException – "Your request was blocked" with custom API base
source_issues.evidence: User reports requests fail with blocked error using SDK with custom base_url, but same API key and endpoint work correctly with direct requests library, suggesting SDK-specific header or behavior issue

signals.topic: Gateway authentication bypass vulnerabilities
signals.summary: Multiple configuration combinations allow unauthenticated access to gateway: Tailscale serve + auth.mode=none, trusted-proxy mode for browser control, *.ts.net Host header spoofing, and WS rate-limiter bypass
signals.review_reason: Users configuring these common combinations (Tailscale serve, trusted-proxy reverse proxy setup) unknowingly expose their gateway. Real user impact: complete loss of intended security boundary when using documented configuration patterns.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Tailscale serve + auth.mode=none exposes gateway to full Tailnet without authentication
source_issues.evidence: Config combination tailscale.mode=serve + auth.mode=none grants full operator access to all Tailnet peers with zero auth

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Browser control server installs no authentication when gateway auth mode is trusted-proxy
source_issues.evidence: trusted-proxy mode starts browser control server with no auth, allowing local processes to execute arbitrary JavaScript in active browser sessions

source_issues.title: [Bug]: *.ts.net Host header accepted as local-direct request, bypassing gateway token auth
source_issues.evidence: Any co-resident process can bypass token auth by setting Host: anything.ts.net header

source_issues.title: [Bug]: WS handshake rate-limiter bypassed by synthetic device identity field
source_issues.evidence: Including any device object in WS connect suppresses rate limiting for failed auth attempts

signals.topic: Session compaction breaks chat.history - stale transcript returned
signals.summary: After session compaction rotates sessionId, the sessionFile field is not updated, causing chat.history and Control UI to return stale/wrong message history from old transcripts instead of current ones
signals.review_reason: High-impact bug causing data integrity failure in core feature. Users see completely wrong message history after compaction - a blocking issue for anyone relying on chat.history or Control UI dashboard to view conversation history. Requires manual workaround script to fix.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: sessionFile not updated after compaction — chat.history returns stale transcript
source_issues.evidence: User reports 147 stale sessionFile entries, chat.history returning messages from March 11 for a session whose transcript was from March 19 - complete data integrity failure in core session feature

signals.topic: Cron systemEvent jobs timeout after ~960s killing main session agent turns
signals.summary: Cron jobs with sessionTarget:'main' and payload.kind:'systemEvent' are killed by scheduler after ~960 seconds, even though main session turns have no inherent timeout and the agent is actively working
signals.review_reason: Breaks automation workflows that need long-running tasks. Users scheduling cron jobs for multi-step operations (video transcription, web searches, file writes) find their jobs killed mid-execution without recourse.

source_issues.title: Cron systemEvent job times out after ~960s even though agent runs in main session
source_issues.evidence: User's cron jobs fail with 'cron: job execution timed out' after 16 minutes, killing actively working agent tasks - blocks automation workflows

signals.topic: Transcript files grow without bound causing performance and disk issues
signals.summary: Regular session transcript files (~/.openclaw/agents/*/sessions/*.jsonl) grow indefinitely with no pruning, unlike heartbeat sessions which have limits. This increases LLM latency and disk usage over time.
signals.review_reason: Causes degraded performance (larger context = slower LLM calls) and unnecessary disk usage. Users must implement workarounds or wait for more frequent compaction cycles.

source_issues.title: Transcript files grow without bound - no pruning for non-heartbeat sessions
source_issues.evidence: User had to create custom hook to truncate files over 100KB - clear performance impact on users

signals.topic: Mattermost inline buttons broken - interaction endpoint returns 404
signals.summary: Interactive message buttons in Mattermost channels return 404 when clicked. The /mattermost/interactions/default route is not registered even with inlineButtons capability enabled and callbackBaseUrl configured.
signals.review_reason: Feature regression breaking Mattermost inline button functionality. Previously working feature now returns 404, blocking users from interactive workflows in Mattermost channels.

source_issues.title: Mattermost inline buttons: /mattermost/interactions/default returns 404 — route not registered
source_issues.evidence: User confirms feature worked on March 9, broke after gateway update - regression blocking Mattermost integration

signals.topic: Model provider selection incorrectly falls back to OpenAI
signals.summary: User configures Groq API but system intermittently defaults to OpenAI, causing unexpected quota errors and workflow disruption
signals.review_reason: Real user pain: configuration not respected, causing unexpected API errors and cost concerns. User expects Groq but gets OpenAI quota errors, disrupting intended workflow with workaround requiring restart.

source_issues.evidence: User explicitly configured Groq model but received OpenAI quota error: 'i wanted it use grooq model. but its by default its using open ai model some time...'

signals.topic: macOS background service keyboard.write failure
signals.summary: interpreter.computer.keyboard.write method fails when run by macOS background services due to NSPasteboard access issues
signals.review_reason: Blocks legitimate automation/background service use cases. User attempting IT policy remediation demo cannot use keyboard.write in background context, with no fallback to character-by-character typing.

source_issues.evidence: AttributeError in keyboard.write when run via fleetd background service: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'declareTypes_owner_' - NSPasteboard.generalPasteboard returns None

signals.topic: Windows startup crash - Git config lock permission denied
signals.summary: Users on Windows encounter OSError when Aider tries to write git config, specifically attempting to create .git/config.lock in system32 directory where users lack write permissions
signals.review_reason: Complete startup failure on Windows - users cannot use Aider at all when this occurs. The application attempts to write git config in a protected system directory, causing immediate crash during initialization.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in util.py line 1054
source_issues.evidence: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: 'C:\\WINDOWS\\system32\\.git\\config.lock' - Application crashes on startup when git tries to acquire config lock

source_issues.title: ffff
